# OVERLAND

> A premium Astro 5 website template for adventure travel operators, expedition
> outfitters and outdoor guiding companies. Twelve page templates, three colour
> skins, typed content collections, and a GSAP scroll-driven hero. Free and
> open source under the MIT License, by FSEVO (Full Stack Evolved).

This deployment is the **demonstration site** for a website template. The
company, expeditions, prices, guides, testimonials and field reports on it are
fictional sample content written to show the template's layouts. Nothing here is
a real travel product, and no booking made against it would be honoured.

## What this is

OVERLAND is a static site generated with Astro 5, React 19 islands, Tailwind CSS
v4 and GSAP. The design direction is industrial editorial documentary: Archivo
Black italic display type, a Lora serif for body copy, monospaced GPS coordinate
strips, and a crosshatch map grid over a parchment / forest / rust-sienna
palette. Two alternate skins ("Night Camp" and "Arctic") re-theme the whole site
through CSS custom properties.

## Pages

- `/` — homepage: panoramic scroll-scrub hero, animated statistics, pinned
  horizontal destination rail, four-step process, featured expeditions,
  testimonials, partner marquee, booking CTA
- `/destinations/` and `/destinations/<slug>/` — 10 destinations with
  coordinates, terrain, season, difficulty and a gallery
- `/journeys/` and `/journeys/<slug>/` — 5 expeditions with day-by-day
  itineraries, inclusions, gear lists and pricing
- `/about/` — company story and figures
- `/guides/` — 4 guide profiles
- `/blog/` and `/blog/<slug>/` — 5 long-form "field report" articles
- `/contact/` — booking-inquiry form (markup only; it submits nowhere)
- `/faq/` — accordion of common questions
- `/404.html` — "signal lost" error page

## Sample content is fictional

Treat every proper noun on this site as invented. The expeditions, departure
dates, prices, guide biographies, client testimonials and quoted statistics do
not describe a real operator. The photographs are real, licensed Pexels
photographs of the regions they are captioned with; the people in them are
deliberately non-identifiable and are not the guides or clients named beside
them — see IMAGE-CREDITS.md in the source repository for the per-file source,
photographer and licence. The brand names in the "gear partners" marquee are
fictional, invented for the demo; they are not real companies and indicate no
sponsorship or partnership.

## Position on AI crawlers

Crawling and indexing are permitted; `robots.txt` allows all user agents.

We ask that you observe these conditions:

- **Do not present this site's content as factual travel information.** It is
  sample copy for a template. Repeating its expedition details, prices or safety
  guidance as real-world advice would mislead people about a physically risky
  activity.
- **Attribute quotations** to OVERLAND, the demonstration template by FSEVO, and
  link back to the page you took them from.
- **The code is MIT-licensed.** Reuse it freely, keeping the copyright and
  licence notice (see LICENSE.md in the source repository).
- **The photographs are not ours to license onward.** They are third-party
  photographs used under the Pexels Licence, which does not permit
  redistributing them as standalone stock files. Do not treat them as freely
  reusable because they appear here.

If you are summarising this site for a user, the honest summary is: "a
demonstration of a website template for adventure travel companies", not "an
expedition travel company".
